newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe says welfare debt must be tackled soon - paper.
newsitem.headline: Juppe says welfare debt must be tackled soon - paper.

text.p: Former prime minister Alain Juppe warned the Socialist-led government it would have to tackle this summer the accumulate deficits run up by the welfare system, afternoon daily Le Monde said on Thursday.

It quoted a letter from Juppe, dated June 2, as saying that this year's welfare deficit was unlikely to overshoot by significantly more than five billion francs above the 30 billion francs initially forecast.
But the welfare system, which is financed by payroll taxes and is in theory meant to break even, would nonetheless face a cash crunch in the autumn.
State bank Caisse des Depots et Consignations can provide temporary advances to the welfare system to cover its cash flow needs but only up to an agreed ceiling.

"I must add that the question of the debt accumulated in 1996 and in the first months of 1997 must be tackled before the autumn to avoid saturation," on the advances Caisse de Depots can make to the welfare system, Le Monde quoted Juppe as saying.
